summary: WP-001 through WP-004 reviewed line-by-line across all four Review Dimensions. All changes are clean, consistent, and architecturally sound.

ShowSnippetTranslation.php (WP-001): The stub is a structurally superior version of BreakTranslation — it adds an explanatory docblock clarifying why the command is unsupported. Strict types declared, correct namespace (Mailcode\Translator\Syntax\HubL), correct base class (BaseHubLCommandTranslation), correct interface (Mailcode_Translator_Command_ShowSnippet), and the stub message follows the established format '{# !<command> is not supported in HubL! #}'. BaseSyntax::createTranslator() throws Mailcode_Translator_Exception on missing class (confirmed at line 47-49 of BaseSyntax.php) — the stub is architecturally required, not optional.

translate-hubl.md (WP-002): showsnippet added to the 'not supported' list with an accurate two-sentence explanation covering DictionaryTool dependency and the stub comment behavior. Consistent with the existing {break} entry format.

mailcode-documentation.md (WP-003): Prerequisite blockquote at line 436 is well-positioned (before the first code example), uses the established '> **Prerequisite:**' format, correctly names DictionaryTool and Apache Velocity, and explicitly flags HubL inability. No false claims.

constraints.md (WP-004): showsnippet correctly absent from HubL partial-coverage list. The pre-existing underdocumentation (6 listed vs 17 actual HubL files) is confirmed but is out-of-scope for this WP and was already tracked by QA.
PHPStan level 9: 0 errors. Test suite: 519/519 pass. No regressions.

comments.note: No HubL-specific ShowSnippet test file exists at tests/testsuites/Translator/HubL/. Third consecutive pipeline (Developer, QA, Reviewer) to flag this. The stub is now the permanent intended behavior; a HubLShowSnippetTests.php asserting the exact stub string for all 6 command variants would guard against silent regression if the stub is ever accidentally replaced with real logic. Recommend creating a follow-up WP.

ShowSnippetTranslation.php docblock is richer than BreakTranslation.php — it explicitly states why the command cannot be translated (no server-side dictionary infrastructure in HubL) and cross-references BreakTranslation as the canonical pattern. This is a positive quality delta worth carrying forward as a convention for future stub classes.

constraints.md HubL coverage (line 64) lists 6 commands against the 17 files confirmed in Translator/Syntax/HubL/. This pre-existing manifest debt should be resolved in a dedicated manifest audit WP that enumerates all HubL classes and separates 'fully translated' from 'stub/unsupported' categories. Independently confirmed by QA on WP-001 and WP-004.

Architectural note: BaseSyntax::createTranslator() (lines 47-49) throws hard on any missing translation class. A future isCommandSupported() hook or an unsupported-commands registry would allow unsupported commands to fall back gracefully without requiring empty stub files. This eliminates the conceptual friction of files whose only purpose is to exist.
